neighbours.label: a sufficiency construction predicting 'do/work/the trick' (any X will [do], did [the] trick)
fire: You don't need fancy tools; an old butter knife will do.
I had a headache, but a cup of strong coffee did the trick.
Any cheap glue stick will work for this kids' craft.
A few drops of vinegar usually do the trick on hard water stains.
No need for a mixer, a simple whisk will do just fine.
When the door squeaks, a little oil does the trick.
If you lack a rolling pin, a wine bottle will work.
For cleaning the grill, crumpled foil will do the job.
quiet: You don't need fancy tools; an old butter knife will arrive tomorrow.
I had a headache, but a cup of strong coffee kept me awake.
Any cheap glue stick will dry out if you leave the cap off.
A few drops of vinegar usually smell strong in a small kitchen.
No need for a mixer, a simple whisk is in the drawer.
When the door squeaks, my cat runs under the bed.
If you lack a rolling pin, a store nearby sells them.
For cleaning the grill, my father wakes up early on Sundays.
